summary: Workers 40 or older get 21 days to consider a severance offer, or 45 in a group layoff.
realLife: The EEOC explains that older workers must get at least 21 days, or 45 for group programs, and may sign earlier only if it is truly their choice. After signing they have 7 days to change their mind.
sources: U.S. EEOC, Q&A on waivers of discrimination claims in severance agreements: https://www.eeoc.gov/laws/guidance/qa-understanding-waivers-discrimination-claims-employee-severance-agreements
inGame: needs: severance agreements and the revocation window; the person's age is on the person record. Scene: needs a producer for layoff-terms.

turns.summary: The person signs in the meeting without using the review time.
pulledBy: a person who is stunned or trusting
turns.writesBack: The terms are fixed, and regret may follow in the mood.

turns.summary: The person takes the whole review period and has the paper read by someone they trust.
pulledBy: a friend or relative who knows the rules
turns.writesBack: The tie to the helper gets closer, and the terms may be bargained.

turns.summary: The employer asks for an answer in a few days despite the review time.
turns.writesBack: The person pushes back or gives in, and the tie to the employer cools.
